requirements.text: В программе есть команда `export --csv <file>`, которая записывает все сохранённые объявления в CSV-файл.
requirements.taskQuote: Add a command `export --csv <file>` to the CLI that writes all saved listings to a CSV file.

requirements.text: В CSV ровно столбцы id, title, price, currency, url, saved_at.
requirements.taskQuote: Columns: id, title, price, currency, url, saved_at.

requirements.text: Цены с двумя знаками после запятой; файл в UTF-8 со строкой заголовков.
requirements.taskQuote: Prices with two decimals, UTF-8 with a header row.

requirements.text: Команда работает на Windows и macOS, а существующие команды не меняются.
requirements.taskQuote: It must work on Windows and macOS and must not change the existing commands.

requirements.text: Для новой команды есть тесты, README обновлён.
requirements.taskQuote: Add tests for the new command and update the README.

lenses.title: Поведение по заданию
lenses.duty: Найти каждый случай, когда новая команда выдаёт неверный результат или падает: столбцы, формат чисел, кодировка, экранирование, пустые данные, ошибки.
procedure: Read the new command's code from argument parsing to the written file.
Run the command on the sample data into your job folder and open the result.
Compare the output with the task line by line: column names and order, two-decimal prices, UTF-8, header row.
Try the cases the code must handle: no saved listings, commas, quotes and line breaks inside titles, non-Latin characters, a missing or unwritable output path.
checklist: Are the columns exactly the ones the task lists, in that order?
Are prices written with two decimals in every case?
Is the file UTF-8 with a header row?
Are commas, quotes and line breaks in values escaped correctly?
Does the command handle an empty list and a bad output path with a clear error?
Does any existing command change its behaviour?

minimum.rule: Every source file, with the new command traced from start to end.
Run the command on the sample data and inspect the output.

lenses.title: Windows, macOS и старые команды
lenses.duty: Найти всё, что сломает новую команду на Windows или macOS или изменит поведение уже существующих команд.
procedure: Read every place the code builds paths, writes files or spawns processes, and check it on both systems (separators, drive letters, spaces and non-Latin names, line endings).
Compare the existing commands before and after the change with the diff source and list every changed line outside the new command.
Run the full test suite and record the output.
checklist: Are paths built with the platform's path functions, never by string concatenation?
Are line endings in the CSV defined and the same on both systems?
Do file names with spaces or non-Latin characters work?
Is any existing command's code or output changed?
Does the full test suite pass?

minimum.rule: Every source file: paths, file writes, processes.
The package manifest: scripts and engines.
The diff of the change and the full test run.

lenses.title: Тесты
lenses.duty: Найти каждое требуемое заданием поведение, которое не проверяет ни один тест, и каждый тест, который пройдёт даже при неверном поведении.
procedure: List every requirement of the task and every edge case the code handles.
For each, find the test that checks it and read its assertions.
Mark tests whose assertions would still pass if the output were wrong (for example checking only that a file exists).
checklist: Is every column and the header row checked by a test?
Is the two-decimal price format checked, including whole numbers?
Are escaping and non-Latin characters checked?
Is the empty-list case checked?
Do the tests run on both systems (no hard-coded paths)?

lenses.title: README и справка
lenses.duty: Найти каждое место, где README или справка команды расходятся с тем, что делает код, или не говорят того, что нужно пользователю.
procedure: Read the README section about the new command and the command's help text.
Compare every option, column, example and default with the code.
Run the documented example as written and compare the result with the README.
checklist: Does the README describe the new command with its exact syntax?
Do the documented columns and format match the code?
Does the documented example run as written?
Is the help text consistent with the README?
Is the language of the README correct and clear?

lenses.title: Первый читатель
lenses.duty: Прочитать всю работу как человек, у которого есть только задание владельца, и найти, где работа не даёт того, что просили, трудна для понимания или в ней нет чего-то нужного.
procedure: Read the owner's task and list everything it asks for.
Read every file of the change once, start to end.
For each thing the task asks for, find where the work delivers it, and note what is missing or only partly there.
checklist: Is every requirement of the task delivered?
Could a new user run the command from the README alone?
Do code, tests and README agree with each other?
Is anything required missing?
Is anything confusing on first reading?

minimum.rule: Read every file once, start to end.
